In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

A defence has been raised by insurance company in the cross-examination of PW-1 by suggesting that the petitioner contributed to the accident in as much as neither the driver of the scooty nor the petitioner were wearing any helmet.
This suggestion has not been denied.
It has also been suggested to PW-1 that he and the driver of the scooty were intoxicated at the time of accident.
This suggestion has been denied by PW-1.
Further, there is nothing in the MLC or discharge summary or any other medical document to show that the petitioner or the driver of the scooty were under influence of alcohol.
Suggestion qua driving licence of petitioner has also been put in the cross- examination.

In the considered opinion of the court, mere not wearing of helmet did not contribute to the occurrence of the accident, which is proved to have been caused due to negligence on the part of respondent no.1.

Similarly, the plea that the driver of the motorbike on which petitioner was riding,
did not have a valid driving licence is not a fact that contributed to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.

Whether or not petitioner, being simplicitor a pillion rider, had a driving licence is immaterial to MACT NO.369/18 Gaurav Rawat v. Kalyan Singh P.No. 6 Of 22 BK the case as he was not the one who was driving the scooty.

As regards loss of income, petitioner has claimed to be working as Manager in M/s. New Impression Shoes and earning Rs.15,450/- p.m.
The income as well as the employment of the petitioner has been disputed by the insurance company.
Petitioner has examined one Rashid Atiq as PW-2 to prove that such PW-2 was employer of PW-1.
PW-2 has testified to be proprietor of New Impression Shoes and claimed that the petitioner/PW-1 was working a Manager in his company since 8- 9 months @ monthly salary of Rs.15,450/-.
During cross- examination, PW-2 has failed to produce any document to show that he is proprietor of any such company or firm.
No record of the company or ledger account has been filed.
Even the salary slips filed on record are neither attested nor certified with any signatures of the employer or stamp of the company.
Such salary slip does not even mention the designation or any other detail of the employee/petitioner.
It is doubtful that while the employer as allegedly issuing salary slips to the petitioner, he was paying salary to the petitioner in cash.
Further, during his cross- examination, PW-2 has stated that that the petitioner was on duty in his shop on the date of accident i.e. 31.12.2017 from 9.30 AM to 8.30 PM.

This fact is contradictory to the averment that the MACT NO.369/18 Gaurav Rawat v. Kalyan Singh P.No. 11 Of 22 BK accident took place at 6.50 PM, when the petitioner would have been working in the shop.
As such, PW-2 is not a reliable witness and the alleged salary slip filed by him cannot be taken as a proof of employment or income/salary of the petitioner.
Further, petitioner has claimed himself to be 10th passed, however, has not filed any proof of his educational qualification.
He is thus assumed to be an unskilled labour working at minimum wages prevalent in Delhi at the time of accident.
The minimum wages of an unskilled labour in Delhi as on 31.12.2017 were Rs.13,584/-.
As per record, petitioner was referred to Batra hospital on 31.12.2017 where he was diagnosed with Degloving injury with bones and muscles and vasculetase exposed on the right thigh.
